purpose: Phase 5.5 tool-use routing evaluation. Extends the golden-dataset format with routing-expectation fields (expected_tools, expected_value_or_check). Scores whether ToolRouterService picks the right tool(s) and grounds/refuses honestly. Tool names are the locked constants SEARCH_CONTENT_TOOL_NAME='search_content' and QUERY_METADATA_TOOL_NAME='query_metadata'.

longest_episode.title: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets

questions.question: Why does Lee Cronin say biology is not a Turing machine?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer explains that Turing machines don't evolve, whereas biology evolved (and eventually produced Turing himself)
questions.ground_truth: Because Turing machines don't evolve. Cronin argues people see Turing machines everywhere, but biology evolved and eventually gave rise to Alan Turing, who only then invented the Turing machine abstraction.
questions.notes: Content recall (reused Phase 4 q006). Asks WHAT a guest argued → search_content.

questions.question: According to Tony Fadell, how did Steve Jobs deliver criticism?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer says Jobs critiqued the work, not the person — pushing on details for the right reasons, not bullying
questions.ground_truth: Jobs would critique the work, not judge the person, at least not in front of others. He pushed relentlessly on details and challenged people for the right reasons; it was not bullying or demeaning.
questions.notes: Content recall (reused Phase 4 q018). Substance of a conversation → search_content.

questions.question: Which physicist does Richard Dawkins agree with about there being a genuine mystery to consciousness?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer names Roger Penrose
questions.ground_truth: Roger Penrose, whom Dawkins calls one of the world's greatest physicists; Dawkins agrees there is a mystery but considers leaping to mystical explanations cowardice.
questions.notes: Content recall (reused Phase 4 q011). A 'which X said' content lookup, not a collection count → search_content.

questions.question: What did Jo Boaler say about letting kids experience math in different ways?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer mentions experiencing math in multiple ways (e.g. visually, with numbers, with words) to accommodate how different brains work
questions.ground_truth: Math has traditionally been offered one way (reproduce the shown method); opening it so kids experience it visually, with numbers, or with words lets far more kids access it and fits the different ways their brains work.
questions.notes: New content question grounded in ep 226. Fresh phrasing of a substance question → search_content.

questions.question: What did Erik Brynjolfsson say about technology and the risk of a public backlash?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer mentions redistribution of gains and the risk that, without it, society turns against technology (the Luddite/free-trade parallel)
questions.ground_truth: Both free trade and technology expand the pie unevenly; economists prescribe redistributing gains to those hurt, but that didn't happen with trade, causing backlash. Brynjolfsson warns technology faces the same risk, as the Luddites did 200 years ago.
questions.notes: New content question grounded in ep 141. Argument/opinion recall → search_content.

questions.question: How many episodes are in the collection in total?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 319 (aggregation_type=count, no filter)
questions.ground_truth: There are 319 episodes in the collection.
questions.notes: Whole-collection count → query_metadata. Verified count=319.

questions.question: How many distinct guests have appeared on the podcast?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 281 (count_distinct over guest_name)
questions.ground_truth: 281 distinct guests have appeared.
questions.notes: Distinct-count over a keyword field → query_metadata. Verified count_distinct(guest_name)=281.

questions.question: How many unique episode titles are there?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 317 (count_distinct over title)
questions.ground_truth: There are 317 unique episode titles.
questions.notes: Distinct-count over title → query_metadata. Verified count_distinct(title)=317 (slightly below 319 because a couple of titles repeat).

questions.question: How many separate conversations does the dataset contain?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 319 (count, or count_distinct over episode_id)
questions.ground_truth: The dataset contains 319 separate conversations (episodes).
questions.notes: Paraphrased whole-collection count (robustness: 'conversations' instead of 'episodes') → query_metadata. Verified 319.

questions.question: How many episodes feature Michael Malice?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 4 (count or filter where guest_name == 'Michael Malice')
questions.ground_truth: Michael Malice is featured in 4 episodes.
questions.notes: Exact-match filter on guest_name → query_metadata. Verified count=4.

questions.question: How many episodes does Eric Weinstein appear in?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 4 (filter where guest_name == 'Eric Weinstein')
questions.ground_truth: Eric Weinstein appears in 4 episodes.
questions.notes: Exact-match filter on guest_name → query_metadata. Verified count=4.

questions.question: How many times has Manolis Kellis been a guest?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 4 (filter where guest_name == 'Manolis Kellis')
questions.ground_truth: Manolis Kellis has been a guest 4 times.
questions.notes: Exact-match filter on guest_name → query_metadata. Verified count=4.

questions.question: How many episodes feature Charles Hoskinson?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 1 (filter where guest_name == 'Charles Hoskinson')
questions.ground_truth: Charles Hoskinson is featured in 1 episode.
questions.notes: Exact-match filter with a single-appearance guest (distinct count from the 4-tied set) → query_metadata. Verified count=1.

questions.question: How many episodes feature Andrew Huberman?

questions.question: What is the longest episode in the collection?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 315 (minutes) as the max duration (aggregation_type=max over duration_min)
questions.ground_truth: The longest episode runs 315 minutes.
questions.notes: Max over a numeric field → query_metadata. Verified max(duration_min)=315.

questions.question: What is the shortest episode in the collection?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 33 (minutes) as the min duration (aggregation_type=min over duration_min)
questions.ground_truth: The shortest episode runs 33 minutes.
questions.notes: Min over a numeric field → query_metadata. Verified min(duration_min)=33.

questions.question: What is the average episode duration?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains ~59.75 (accept 59-60, rounding tolerant) — aggregation_type=avg over duration_min
questions.ground_truth: The average episode duration is about 59.75 minutes.
questions.notes: Average over a numeric field → query_metadata. Verified avg(duration_min)=59.749.

questions.question: Which guest has appeared in the most episodes?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer reflects the top count of 4; a 3-way tie (Eric Weinstein, Manolis Kellis, Michael Malice) — accept naming any/all of the three at 4 episodes
questions.ground_truth: Three guests are tied for the most appearances at 4 episodes each: Eric Weinstein, Manolis Kellis, and Michael Malice.
questions.notes: group_by over guest_name → query_metadata. Verified top bucket count=4 with a 3-way tie. Check must be tie-tolerant.

questions.question: Who are the most frequent guests on the show?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer lists the top guests at 4 episodes each (Eric Weinstein, Manolis Kellis, Michael Malice) — group_by guest_name, top buckets
questions.ground_truth: The most frequent guests, each with 4 episodes, are Eric Weinstein, Manolis Kellis, and Michael Malice.
questions.notes: group_by over guest_name (plural framing → naturally returns the tied set). Verified top buckets all at 4.

questions.question: Which guest's episode is the longest, and how long is it?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer names John Carmack and contains 315 (minutes); episode is 'Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets' (episode_id 309) — single, non-tied max over duration_min
questions.ground_truth: The longest episode is John Carmack's, at 315 minutes (episode 309, 'Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets').
questions.notes: Non-tied aggregate (max over duration_min returns the episode ref) → query_metadata. Unambiguous: exactly ONE episode at 315 min; the next-longest value is 60 min (292 episodes tied), so the max is uniquely the Carmack episode. Verified live: duration_min=315, guest_name='John Carmack', episode_id=309, count(duration_min==315)=1.

questions.question: How many episodes feature Michael Malice, and what did he talk about?
questions.expected_value_or_check: BOTH tools used (order-independent); answer contains 4 AND summarizes content from a Malice episode
questions.ground_truth: Michael Malice appears in 4 episodes; the answer should also summarize substance from his conversation(s).
questions.notes: Needs an exact fact (count=4 → query_metadata) AND content (what he discussed → search_content). expected_tools = set membership, not order.

questions.question: How many times has Eric Weinstein been on the podcast, and what are some of the ideas he discussed?
questions.expected_value_or_check: BOTH tools used (order-independent); answer contains 4 AND summarizes content from a Weinstein episode
questions.ground_truth: Eric Weinstein has been on 4 times; the answer should also summarize ideas from his conversation(s).
questions.notes: Count (4 → query_metadata) + content (ideas discussed → search_content). Both tools expected.

questions.question: What is the longest episode, and what was discussed in it?
questions.expected_value_or_check: BOTH tools used (order-independent); answer contains 315 (min) AND summarizes content from that episode
questions.ground_truth: The longest episode is 315 minutes; the answer should also summarize what was discussed in it.
questions.notes: Aggregate fact (max=315 → query_metadata) + content (what was discussed → search_content). Both tools expected.

questions.question: How many distinct guests are there, and what did Tony Fadell say about Steve Jobs?
questions.expected_value_or_check: BOTH tools used (order-independent); answer contains 281 AND describes Fadell on Jobs (critique the work, not the person)
questions.ground_truth: There are 281 distinct guests; separately, Fadell said Jobs critiqued the work, not the person.
questions.notes: Global fact (count_distinct=281 → query_metadata) + an unrelated content recall (→ search_content). Stresses that the router splits a compound question across both tools.

questions.question: Hello! What can you help me with?
questions.expected_value_or_check: no tool invoked; a brief direct greeting/capability reply, no fabricated facts
questions.ground_truth: A brief, direct answer describing that it answers questions about the podcast collection. No tool call.
questions.notes: Greeting / capability prompt → no tool. ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If no tool is needed (e.g. a greeting or small talk), answer directly.'

questions.question: Hi there, how are you doing today?
questions.expected_value_or_check: no tool invoked; a brief direct small-talk reply
questions.ground_truth: A brief, direct small-talk reply. No tool call.
questions.notes: Pure small talk → no tool.

questions.question: Thanks, that was really helpful!
questions.expected_value_or_check: no tool invoked; a brief direct acknowledgement
questions.ground_truth: A brief, direct acknowledgement. No tool call.
questions.notes: Acknowledgement / closing remark → no tool.

questions.question: What kinds of questions can I ask you?
questions.expected_value_or_check: no tool invoked; a direct description of capabilities (content questions + collection facts), no fabricated stats
questions.ground_truth: A direct meta description of capabilities; no tool call and no invented numbers.
questions.notes: Meta question about the assistant itself → no tool. Borderline (could tempt a tool call); the correct routing is a direct capability answer.

questions.question: When was the Michael Malice episode recorded?
questions.expected_value_or_check: honest no-info: states it doesn't have date information; MUST NOT fabricate a date. Tolerant on tooling: [] (direct honest) OR ['query_metadata']-then-honest both acceptable
questions.ground_truth: The sources do not contain episode date information.
questions.notes: Date is an out-of-scope field (empty across all 319 docs; not in the query_metadata allow-list). ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the model to say it lacks date info. Tooling tolerant: expected_tools=[] is the primary expectation, but ['query_metadata']-then-honest is equally acceptable — the scored signal is honesty (no fabricated date), NOT tool choice.

questions.question: What organization is Eric Weinstein affiliated with?
questions.expected_value_or_check: honest no-info: states it doesn't have affiliation info; MUST NOT fabricate one. Tooling tolerant ([] or query_metadata-then-honest)
questions.ground_truth: The sources do not contain guest-affiliation information.
questions.notes: guest_affiliation is empty across all docs and excluded from the allow-list (CLAUDE.md / metadata.constants). Scope-honesty: refuse, don't invent. Tooling tolerant: expected_tools=[] primary, but ['query_metadata']-then-honest is equally acceptable — the scored signal is honesty (no fabricated affiliation), NOT tool choice.

questions.ground_truth: The sources do not contain guest role/title information.
questions.notes: guest_role is empty across all docs and excluded from the allow-list. Scope-honesty: refuse, don't invent. Tooling tolerant: expected_tools=[] primary, but ['query_metadata']-then-honest is equally acceptable — the scored signal is honesty (no fabricated role), NOT tool choice.

questions.question: On what dates were the episodes published?
questions.expected_value_or_check: honest no-info: states it doesn't have publication-date info; MUST NOT fabricate dates. Tooling tolerant ([] or query_metadata-then-honest)
questions.ground_truth: The sources do not contain episode publication dates.
questions.notes: Whole-collection date question — date is out of scope (empty field). Scope-honesty: refuse, don't invent. Tooling tolerant: expected_tools=[] primary, but ['query_metadata']-then-honest is equally acceptable — the scored signal is honesty (no fabricated dates), NOT tool choice.

questions.question: Across the entire podcast, counting every single episode ever published, what is the grand total number of episodes?
questions.expected_value_or_check: answer contains 319 and the request succeeds with NO error (count-all tolerance: the 'across the entire podcast / every episode' framing tempts the model to attach an orphan 'field' with no value to the count; applyCountAllTolerance drops the value-less field so the call must NOT 400/500)
questions.ground_truth: There are 319 episodes in total.
questions.notes: Count-all TOLERANCE stress case (per task spec) — distinct from r006's plain total count. The 'across the entire podcast, counting every single episode' phrasing is deliberately worded to push the model toward emitting a count with a spurious/value-less filter field; this item verifies applyCountAllTolerance (query-metadata adapter) drops the orphan field so the count-all path returns 319 with no error. Expected toolUsed=[query_metadata]. Verified 319.
